title: Anticoagulation Monitoring in Critically Ill Patients: Study Protocol
author: Mirus, Martin
materials: Written informed consent by patient or legal representative
LMWH / UFH: EX-, RVV-, RVH-, ECA-test.
Endogenous thrombin potential (ETP; area under the curve)
Time point: As the primary outcome.
Time point: As in primary outcome.
Time point: Parallel to VET and TGA sampling.
Metric: Interaction terms in regression/mixed-effects models; subgroup analyses.

steps.title: Screen and enroll eligible patients
steps.instruction: Identify ICU patients receiving UFH or LMWH, age ≥18 years, and meeting sepsis criteria (sepsis or septic shock within the last 48 h per Sepsis‑3). Exclude those with hereditary coagulation disorders or ongoing therapeutic oral anticoagulants (DOACs or VKAs) unless residual activity can be ruled out. Obtain written informed consent from the patient or legal representative before enrollment.

steps.title: Schedule blood sampling time points
steps.instruction: Plan two blood draws per participant: the first at study inclusion and the second 24–72 h later. For LMWH, schedule the draw 4 h after the last subcutaneous dose to capture peak plasma concentration. For continuous UFH infusion, schedule the draw at steady state, defined as ≥4–6 h after infusion start or after any dose adjustment.

steps.title: Collect arterial blood using discard protocol
steps.instruction: Draw blood from an indwelling arterial catheter using a standardized discard volume to avoid contamination. Use 3.2 % sodium citrate tubes for all coagulation-related samples.

steps.title: Prepare citrated whole blood for viscoelastic testing
steps.instruction: Gently invert the citrate tube, then transfer whole blood to the ClotPro® device within 120 min of collection. Maintain the sample at the temperature recommended by the manufacturer (controlled room temperature as per ClotPro® SOP).

steps.title: Process plasma for biochemical assays
steps.instruction: Within 60 min of collection, centrifuge citrate tubes using pre‑programmed settings in a designated laboratory area. Aliquot the supernatant plasma into 300 µL polypropylene tubes and store temporarily at –80 °C for later batch analysis. This minimizes platelet contamination and stabilises labile markers such as PF1 + 2, TAT and TGA parameters.

steps.title: Perform routine laboratory analyses
steps.instruction: Transport samples to the central laboratory. Run the following assays on a STAGO coagulation platform (Diagnostica Stago, France): Quick/INR, aPTT, chromogenic Anti‑Xa (no exogenous antithrombin added), antithrombin, D‑dimers, fibrinogen, factor VIII (UFH patients only), factor XIII, platelet count, creatinine, urea, estimated GFR, ASAT, ALAT, bilirubin, triglycerides, albumin. Re‑measure routine biochemistry and inflammatory markers (CRP, procalcitonin) only if the last clinical result is >24 h old.

steps.title: Conduct viscoelastic testing on ClotPro
steps.instruction: At the bedside, log the patient ID, select the appropriate cartridge and test channel, and scan the pipette tip. Load citrated whole blood into the test cup, mix gently, and start the measurement. Perform the following assays according to anticoagulant type: EX, RVV, RVH, ECA for both LMWH and UFH; add IN/HI for UFH. Record clotting time (CT), clot formation time (CFT), amplitudes at 5 and 10 min (A5, A10), maximum clot firmness (MCF), alpha angle, lysis time (LT), maximum lysis (ML). Document the elapsed time from sampling to test initiation.

steps.title: Run thrombin generation assay
steps.instruction: Use platelet‑poor plasma on the Innovance® ETP assay (Siemens Healthineers) with a BCS XP analyser. Initiate coagulation by adding tissue factor, phospholipids and calcium according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Record endogenous thrombin potential (ETP), peak thrombin, lag time, and time to peak thrombin generation. The software automatically corrects for α2‑macroglobulin‑bound thrombin activity.

steps.title: Execute ELISA assays for advanced markers
steps.instruction: Perform ELISAs in duplicate for the following markers using the indicated kits: Plasmin‑antiplasmin complexes (PAP, Cloud‑Clone Corp.), Plasminogen activator inhibitor‑1 (PAI‑1, Technozym®), Tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI, Cloud‑Clone Corp.), Thrombin‑antithrombin complexes (TAT, Cloud‑Clone Corp.), Prothrombin fragments 1 + 2 (PF1 + 2, Cloud‑Clone Corp.). Include a standard curve in each run and conduct batch analysis to reduce inter‑assay variability.

steps.title: Perform arterial blood gas analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the arterial sample for calcium, haemoglobin and haematocrit values at the time of each blood draw.

steps.title: Record clinical variables and modifiers
steps.instruction: Document sepsis status, SOFA score, renal function (creatinine, eGFR), albumin, BMI, inflammatory markers (CRP, fibrinogen), and any other predefined effect‑modifier variables for later statistical modelling.

steps.title: Store and manage samples for batch analysis
steps.instruction: After aliquoting, keep plasma samples at –80 °C until the scheduled batch run. Ensure that residual blood is discarded in designated biohazard containers.

steps.title: Implement quality control for point‑of‑care devices
steps.instruction: Perform weekly quality‑control checks on the ClotPro® device according to the manufacturer’s specifications. Verify that all test channels and cartridges pass QC before patient testing.

steps.title: Determine target sample size and power
steps.instruction: Based on published data (r = 0.669, p = 0.0395) and assuming a conservative effect size of r = 0.6 for UFH, calculate required independent pairs using G*Power 3.1 (α = 0.05, power = 0.80): 19 pairs for r = 0.669 and 23 pairs for r = 0.6. Adjust for repeated measures with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.3, giving a design effect of 1.54 (≈1.54 independent observations per patient). This yields a minimum of 13 LMWH‑treated and 15 UFH‑treated patients. Allowing for a 15 % dropout, set the recruitment target to 30 LMWH‑treated and 36 UFH‑treated patients (total n = 66).

steps.title: Analyze data according to statistical plan
steps.instruction: Use a linear mixed‑effects model with a random intercept for patient and a fixed effect for anticoagulant type to assess the primary correlation between Anti‑Xa activity and CT‑RVV. Report regression slopes per 0.1 IU/mL Anti‑Xa with 95 % CIs. Additionally compute Spearman rank correlations (with bootstrap 95 % CIs) for the overall cohort and stratified by anticoagulant. Perform Passing‑Bablok regression to evaluate proportional (slope CI includes 1.0) and constant bias (intercept CI includes 0). For secondary outcomes, calculate Spearman correlations between VET parameters (CFT, A5, A10, MCF, α‑angle, LT, ML) and Anti‑Xa/TGA variables, and run multivariable mixed‑effects regressions including pre‑specified effect modifiers (sepsis status, antithrombin, renal function, inflammatory markers). Apply Benjamini‑Hochberg false‑discovery‑rate correction within each predefined parameter family. Conduct dose‑exposure‑response analyses with linear and non‑linear mixed‑effects models, testing interaction terms for age, sex, renal function, SOFA, SAPS II. Summarise baseline characteristics as counts/percentages or mean ± SD (or median [IQR] if non‑normal). Perform all analyses in SPSS v27 and RStudio (version 2025.05.0 + 496); consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.

steps.title: Maintain data security and documentation
steps.instruction: Store all patient data, laboratory results and analysis files on the secure institutional network of the University Hospital Dresden. Ensure that only authorized study personnel have access and that data are backed up regularly.
